newsitem.title: CANADA: Poet Ginsberg not upset by bank's use of Dylan song.
newsitem.headline: Poet Ginsberg not upset by bank's use of Dylan song.

text.p: Poet Allen Ginsberg, a sometime collaborator with folk icon Bob Dylan, has dismissed criticism by baby boomers angered by the use of Dylan's protest anthem, "The Times They are a-Changin" as a Canadian bank jingle.
"I think Bob Dylan is such a genius survivor and I hope he gets the Nobel Prize," Ginsberg, 70, said at a recent poetry reading in Toronto. "That'll pay him more than the bank."
Ginsberg appeared in a mid-1960s video of Dylan's "Subterranean Homesick Blues" and worked on some songs with him.
Bank of Montreal, Canada's third biggest bank, recently began airing controversial television ads featuring children running down country roads and across lush fields as a choir sings Dylan's song.
The bank has not disclosed how much it paid for the rights to the tune.
Canadian newspapers were swamped with letters from baby boomers disturbed by the bank's use of the 1964 song that many remember as a symbol of their youthful ideals.
Canada's banks, set to report a third straight year of record earnings, are hugely unpopular among many consumers, angry about high service fees and tight lending policies.
Critics find it ironic that a bank would use a song that warns: "You better start swimming or you'll sink like a stone."
A letter to Toronto's Globe and Mail newspaper sarcastically reworked Dylan's lyrics as a cynical appeal to former flower children.
"Come latter-day hippies, please heed the call. You're all pre-approved at the Bank of Montreal," the letter said.
Ginsberg, who is on tour to promote his "Selected Poems 1947-1995", said he had not seen the ads, but would watch for them while in Canada.
Best known for his long poem "Howl", Ginsberg has appeared in Gap clothing ads, but said he donated his earnings to The Naropa Institute, a school he started in Colorado.
He noted that author William S. Burroughs appeared in a Nike ad.
"With Burroughs, it was more a case of Nike advertising him," Ginsberg said.
